title: Convergence and the Riemann hypothesis
venue: Communications of the Korean Mathematical Society11(1)(1996),57–62
version: Official publisher scan, six printed pages57–62; received1995-09-13, revised1995-09-26; publisher printing date1996-03-01
read_scope: Complete six-page primary text read; main theoremp59 and central proofpp60–61 visually checked. No full technical verification; p61 scan partly streaked but displayed mathematical passages readable.
main_result: For fixed1<p<=2, zero-free Re(s)>1/p iff the prescribed unsmoothed fractional-part sums sum_(n<=N)mu(n){1/(nx)} converge to−1 in every fixedL^r(0,1),1<r<p; equivalent density statements for constrained real/rational Beurling generators. Main unnumbered theoremp59; constrained correction Eq2p60.
limitations: Endpoint r=p is excluded; no L²-boundary convergence is claimed at p2.
No moving logarithmic Riesz weights or shifted n^−epsilon array appears.
Printed infinite Perron absolute-majorant integralp59 diverges as written; no L2 audit or false-main-theorem claim is made.
No DOI supplied in inspected publisher metadata; absence is not a proof no DOI exists.
Priority of the archive moving-array construction remains unassessed.

title: Riesz summability on boundary lines of holomorphic functions of finite order generated by Dirichlet series
version: Actual text read arXivv3,2022-03-22; journal metadata verified but mathematical journal version not compared
read_scope: Definitions pp2–3; selected introduction/classical comparisons pp6–10; exact Perron formula/kernel and boundary theorem pp15–18, including Theorems1.2,4.1,5.1. Not whole38-page manuscript or complete proof audit.
main_result_in_inspected_scope: Fixed k>ell boundary Riesz convergence for general-frequency germs with uniform sup_(Re>0)|f/(1+s)^ell| finite; exact gamma/Perron kernel. Classical finite-boundary-pole theorem recalled separately.
limitations: Reciprocal zeta shifted to the critical boundary fails the uniform growth hypothesis near every boundary zero.
The fixed-order theorem and recalled finitely-many-pole theorem are not claimed to imply the moving-array weighted product norm.
No publication novelty conclusion; original Riesz1909 not read.

title: On Divergence of Fourier Series by Some Methods of Summability
venue: Journal of Function Spaces and Applications2012,article542607,9pages
version: Actual primary typeset article; downloaded file has nine article pages and one unrelated advertisement page
read_scope: Introduction/triangular-matrix definitions; Theorems1.3–1.4 and proof excerpts pp5–7; Remark2.4 pp8–9. Not full proof audit.
main_result_in_inspected_scope: Variable arithmetic Riesz orders are explicitly defined in Remark2.4. The compared divergence statements have alpha_n<=C/log n with C<log2, hence vanishing order.
limitations: Arithmetic frequency and vanishing order differ from the growing logarithmic order of the investigated array.
Fourier divergence examples do not provide a Mobius weighted boundary-norm criterion.

title: On the Wintner-Ingham-Segal summability method
version: Actual eight-page journal text; printed volume year2018, Crossref online date2019-01-23
read_scope: Initial definitions and assumptions pp40–41; Proposition3.2, smoothing identities3.18–3.19, Theorem3.4 and references pp43–47. Intermediate proof estimates not fully audited.
main_result_in_inspected_scope: Ingham arithmetic convolution summability implies fixed F(k/r)-smoothing under the stated shape and PNT-decay assumptions; supplies references to Wintner and Segal originals.
limitations: Fixed arithmetic smoothing does not directly cover an N-dependent logarithmic Riesz order and weighted critical product norm.
Wintner1957 and Segal1975/1977 originals were not read in this investigation.
Volume year and online metadata date distinguished.
